brief: Four-storey brick hotel of 1815-1841 on the main street, the oldest inn in the region: plain Federal walls, a two-tier iron-and-wood gallery across the front on slender posts, a hanging sign, and a dining room on the ground floor. Record: 1 photo plus 8 measured drawing sheets. Modelled at three storeys.

facade.notes: the Golden Lamb (Lebanon OH, 1815/1841), Ohio's oldest inn: a four-storey brick hotel with a dentilled cornice, a two-storey columned and balustraded gallery over the sidewalk, a hanging sign, an iron fire escape; 1930s cars at the curb

why.note: hotels got fire escapes after the 1900s fire laws
